anti_overlap: Does not evaluate atproto/DID auth mechanics or identity lock-in — fd-atproto-identity-lockin owns that
Does not evaluate whether propose-not-move holds up socially — fd-agent-governance-launch-gate owns governance-under-real-dynamics and v1-scope findings
Stays on data-model and scale-bound findings; does not weigh in on visual or rendering aesthetics of regions
decision_lens: Does the Yjs/Postgres split actually hold as regions accumulate and cool, is there a credible compaction or page-out story before build starts, and are the stated scale bounds (~10 humans plus agents, one canvas) grounded in real CRDT doc-size and fan-out numbers rather than assumed?
focus: CRDT/Postgres data-model split and scale bounds for a small persistent spatial canvas
name: fd-crdt-canvas-scale-model
persona: Apply the perspective of a systems architect who has shipped production CRDT-backed multiplayer canvas products (Figma-, tldraw-, Miro-style whiteboards) and knows the operational failure modes of unbounded-growth Yjs documents at scale.
review_areas: Whether Yjs-doc responsibilities (layout, presence, live composition) stay bounded, or message history leaks into the CRDT doc, since cooled regions must stay represented indefinitely
Whether a credible page-out or compaction mechanism for cooled regions (open question 2) exists before build, since Yjs docs degrade past certain operation counts without subdocuments
Whether relay fan-out at '~10 humans' is the real bound, or per-participant tending agents multiply live peer count and update volume well past the stated ceiling
Whether attribution and governance-ledger writes in Postgres stay causally consistent with concurrent Yjs region placement as agents cluster, propose, and move content across both stores
Whether 'zoom is the attention dial' implies a real query/pagination pattern against Postgres, or is currently only a rendering-layer promise with no data-access design behind it
Whether region 'temperature' and per-user read-state high-water marks (open question 3) have one clear home in the Yjs/Postgres split, or risk being computed twice and drifting

severity_examples.condition: No compaction, subdocument, or page-out spec exists before schema/sync code is written.
severity_examples.scenario: The Yjs doc has no snapshotting/subdocument strategy and is expected to hold spatial layout for a canvas whose whole premise is that history never scrolls away; after weeks of real use the doc grows into the hundreds of MB and every client must hydrate all of it to open the canvas, making 'wander back in' — the entire fix for scroll-up pain — the slowest operation in the product.

severity_examples.condition: Scale-bound claims in the doc do not distinguish human peers from agent peers.
severity_examples.scenario: Per-participant tending agents (even the v1 minimum of one house agent per person) are not counted in the '~10 humans' scale bound, so live relay fan-out at launch is actually humans-plus-agents, a multiple of the stated ceiling with no load data behind either number.

severity_examples.condition: No single source of truth named for a value referenced by both the CRDT layer and the ledger.
severity_examples.scenario: Region temperature is implied to drive the zoomed-out 'what's alive' view but the doc does not say whether it is derived from Yjs activity or computed server-side in Postgres, risking two independently-drifting temperature values.

success_hints: Ties each concern to a specific Yjs/CRDT failure pattern (doc bloat, awareness-protocol storms, missing subdocument boundaries), not generic 'scale' hand-waving
Separates genuine spike-first unknowns (e.g. rendering substrate) from load-bearing gaps that block build sequencing (the Yjs/Postgres split itself)
Where the doc gives no number, supplies a rough back-of-envelope one (doc size, message rate, peer count) so the open question becomes falsifiable
task_context: This review targets docs/brainstorms/2026-07-26-infinite-canvas-pivot.md, an adopted brainstorm (epic garden-salon-x9l) pivoting Garden Salon from git-repo collaboration to an infinite-canvas chat space. It carries over packages/salon-core's Yjs relay/presence and the Meadowsyn rendering architecture unchanged, adding topics-as-spatial-regions, atproto auth, and agent tending via propose-not-move governance, for a v1 cohort of about 10 humans plus agents on one canvas. Goal: Stress the adopted pivot design before build phases start: (1) the propose-not-move resolution of agent-reorganization vs spatial memory — does it actually hold under real group-chat dynamics? (2) atproto OAuth + DID identity risks and lock-in; (3) canvas data-model split (Yjs vs Postgres) and scale bounds for a 10-human cohort; (4) v1 scope integrity — what's missing that would block the launch gate (X group chat cohort actually moving in), and what's included that shouldn't be.
